history.note: harness until the mode-cutoff restart (borg-zoo#54). The runner and observer are unchanged at the new pin; the bump keeps the harness commit at the specimens' tree after the 0100/0101/0101a fixes. A proposed runner change that would have recorded the applied configuration text (better-borg-c PR 435) was closed as mis-filed and is not needed: configuration_sha256 already identifies what a run applied.
live watchdog read could abort a run on a split UTF-8 character (better-borg-c#220); fixed by 56ccf741. The observer is unchanged between the two pins.

harness.note: The better-borg-c runner and observer at this commit build and run every specimen. A specimen is the game and Borg source at its own ref; the observer instrumentation comes from the harness commit. It applies to specimens of kind "better-borg-c" (the default). Specimens of kind "borg-rs" are built and run by borg-rs's own harness at the specimen's ref (harness/build.sh and the borgh frontend). This pin is also a specimen ref (4.2.6-bbc-9ca98661): the harness bumped with the mode-cutoff restart so runner and specimens move together (borg-zoo#54).

normal.description: Ordinary play with every mode flag pinned off: no munchkin start, no munchkin by class, no Lunal. The arm every change can be checked against. Only builds that know borg_munchkin_by_class (better-borg-c fd683ced and later) can run it; older builds ignore the unknown setting, the observer cannot verify it, and the run is a config_error.

town-negative.description: The negative baseline for the town inventory redesign (borg-rs#36, borg-zoo#81): the Borg performs no store interaction at all - it never buys, never sells, never uses the home as a stash or a swap source, and never walks into a shop. Everything else is unchanged: it still recalls to town, still equips itself, still dives. A floor, not a candidate strategy: the arm is expected to be worse, and no improvement is claimed in either direction. The four mode flags are pinned off, as in the normal profile, so the only difference from the normal arm is borg_town_no_stores (the issue's profile named the setting alone; borg-rs's default applies the class rule from M8, which would have made Warriors, Druids and Rangers differ from the control in two ways). Needs a build that knows borg_town_no_stores; older builds ignore the unknown setting, the observer cannot verify it, and the run is a config_error.

4.2.6-rs-town.label: borg-rs, the town-inventory redesign branch (feature/town-inventory-strategy) at the negative-baseline commit: the Rust Borg as it stands on the branch, with the new setting borg_town_no_stores exposed (default FALSE, today's behaviour). Rust-only; the C parser accepts the setting and ignores it, so no C parity cell. No derived tag yet - the ref is a branch head (borg-rs#36, PR 42; borg-zoo#81).

classes-18.description: Every class twice: 18 fresh seeds, 100,000 engine turns, classes dealt and races cycled as in classes-1800. A smoke suite for assigned births.

experiment.description: The negative baseline for the town inventory redesign (borg-zoo#81): borg-rs with no store interaction at all, against the same build trading normally, both arms with every mode pinned off. A calibration floor, not a candidate strategy: the arm is expected to be worse and no improvement is claimed in either direction. Prespecified, per class and paired on the seed: character level at 50% and 100% of the cap (milestones[].level) and final.max_depth; secondary: milestones[].gold (must not move), first_turn_at_depth, final.keys, the death split. classes-18 is the pilot (36 cells); the full grid (classes-1800) follows only if the pilot reads well.
experiment.name: town-negative
